sourceEnglishObjective: Check on crew hydration and heat symptoms
sourceEnglishSpeaking: Ask a worker how they feel and direct a water break under the site heat plan.
candidateObjective: 作業員の水分補給と暑さによる症状を確認する。
candidateFocus: ～ごとに gives the hourly interval. ～なら invites a report of symptoms; ～ので connects dizziness with resting in the shade.

archivedForms.exampleJa: ラウルは一時間ごとに水を飲みます。
ラウルはめまいがするので日陰で休みます。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Raúl rests in the shade because he feels dizzy.

archivedForms.exampleJa: ラウル、体調はどう感じますか。
ラウルは気分が悪ければ職長に伝えます。
archivedForms.meaningEnglish: to let know, to tell, to notify
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Raúl tells the foreman if he feels sick.

archivedForms.exampleJa: ラウルは休むために日陰に行きます。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Raúl goes to the shade to rest.

archivedSpeaking.opening: 体調はどうですか。めまいがしますか。日陰に行って休み、今、水を飲んでください。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Ask a worker how they feel and direct a water break under the site heat plan.

curriculumAdaptationNote: Preserve the source scene and clinical vocabulary directly: heat on the roof; the foreman's hourly water-break instruction; Raúl appears unwell; the foreman asks how he feels and whether he is dizzy; Raúl says yes; the foreman directs shade, rest and water, asks for symptom reporting, and commits to the site heat plan; the closing line says hydration and shade rest help prevent heat exhaustion. The archived Reader invents a specific pallor observation. The isolated hourly schedule and response sequence need qualified site heat-plan/clinical review, and 熱疲労 needs a contextual dictionary decision. Current curriculum has no authored verb-example list; archived forms remain conditional evidence. No selected learner/audio text or progress identity is created.

cards.reviewNote: Heat exhaustion / agotamiento por calor is a clinical occupational-heat term. Confirm archived 熱疲労 against the intended Japanese diagnosis/symptom distinction; do not silently substitute broader 熱中症.

cards.sourceEnglish: Take a water break every hour.
cards.archivedJapanese: 一時間ごとに水分補給の休憩を取ってください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Take a water break every hour.
cards.reviewNote: Hourly water breaks are stated in this source scene, while the speaking objective says to act under the site heat plan. Confirm that an isolated card does not imply a universal schedule.

cards.sourceSpanish: Vaya a la sombra y descanse.
cards.sourceEnglish: Go to the shade and rest.
cards.archivedJapanese: 日陰に行って休んでください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Go to the shade and rest.
cards.reviewNote: Shade and rest are direct source commands to a dizzy worker. Keep the words but hold the response sequence for qualified site heat-plan and domain review.

cards.archivedJapanese: 今、水を飲んでください。
cards.reviewNote: Drink water now is a direct source command in the dizziness scene. Confirm how it fits the site heat response and escalation plan before a scored safety instruction.

cards.sourceEnglish: Tell me if you feel sick.
cards.archivedJapanese: 気分が悪ければ教えてください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Tell me if you feel sick.
cards.reviewNote: Source se siente mal means feeling unwell; archived 気分が悪い may be read as nausea or mood. Confirm the symptom-reporting sense and site-plan escalation context.

reader.sourceSpanish: Hace mucho calor y el sol pega fuerte en el techo.
reader.sourceEnglish: It is very hot and the sun beats down on the roof.
reader.candidateJapanese: とても暑く、屋根には強い日差しが照りつけています。
reader.archivedJapanese: とても暑く、屋根には強い日差しが照りつけています。
reader.archivedEnglish: It is very hot and the sun beats down on the roof.

reader.sourceSpanish: El capataz dice: Tomen agua cada hora.
reader.sourceEnglish: The foreman says: Take a water break every hour.
reader.archivedJapanese: 職長は「一時間ごとに水分補給の休憩を取ってください」と言います。
reader.archivedEnglish: The foreman says: Take a water break every hour.
reader.reviewNote: Hourly break is the foreman's instruction in this source scene, not necessarily a universal rule; align it with the site heat plan in the speaking objective.

reader.sourceSpanish: Pero Raúl no se ve bien, y el capataz se acerca.
reader.sourceEnglish: But Raúl does not look well, and the foreman walks over.
reader.archivedJapanese: しかし、ラウルの顔色が悪く見え、職長が近づきます。
reader.archivedEnglish: But Raúl does not look well, and the foreman walks over.
reader.reviewNote: Source says Raúl does not look well; archived 顔色が悪い adds pallor or poor complexion as a specific observation. Remove that invented sign or obtain source approval.

reader.sourceSpanish: El capataz le pregunta: ¿Cómo se siente?
reader.sourceEnglish: The foreman asks him: How do you feel?
reader.candidateJapanese: 職長は「体調はどうですか」と尋ねます。
reader.archivedJapanese: 職長は「体調はどうですか」と尋ねます。
reader.archivedEnglish: The foreman asks him: How do you feel?

reader.reviewNote: The direct dizziness question is accurate in form, but a positive response drives the following safety sequence. Confirm clinical and site-plan linkage before scored deployment.

reader.sourceSpanish: Raúl contesta que sí, un poco.
reader.candidateJapanese: ラウルは「はい、少し」と答えます。
reader.archivedJapanese: ラウルは「はい、少し」と答えます。

reader.sourceSpanish: El capataz le dice: Vaya a la sombra y descanse. Tome agua ahora.
reader.sourceEnglish: The foreman tells him: Go to the shade and rest. Drink water now.
reader.archivedJapanese: 職長は「日陰に行って休んでください。今、水を飲んでください」と伝えます。
reader.archivedEnglish: The foreman tells him: Go to the shade and rest. Drink water now.
reader.reviewNote: Shade, rest and water are source commands to a dizzy worker. Qualified heat-plan review must assess the escalation and symptom-response sequence without erasing the source vocabulary.

reader.sourceSpanish: Avíseme si se siente mal, y vamos a seguir el plan de calor del sitio.
reader.sourceEnglish: Tell me if you feel sick, and we will follow the site heat plan.
reader.archivedJapanese: 「気分が悪ければ教えてください。現場の暑熱対策計画に従います。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Tell me if you feel sick, and we will follow the site heat plan.
reader.reviewNote: Source says we will follow the site heat plan. Archived Japanese present phrasing can obscure the crew commitment; confirm subject, timing and escalation wording.

reader.sourceSpanish: La hidratación y el descanso en la sombra ayudan a evitar el agotamiento por calor.
reader.sourceEnglish: Hydration and rest in the shade help prevent heat exhaustion.
reader.archivedJapanese: 水分補給と日陰での休息は熱疲労の予防に役立ちます。
reader.archivedEnglish: Hydration and rest in the shade help prevent heat exhaustion.
reader.reviewNote: Hydration and shade rest help prevent heat exhaustion is the source's factual claim. Qualified occupational-heat/clinical review must confirm its scope and Japanese 熱疲労 sense.

see.label: Find the water, shade, and crew member feeling dizzy.

recall.label: Recall dizziness, heat exhaustion, hydration, and rest.

hear.label: Distinguish めまい from 熱疲労 when spoken.

say.label: Ask how a crew member feels and mention water and shade.

write.label: Write how the foreman follows the site heat plan.
